topSignals.title: FERC RM26-4 open meeting today — large-load interconnection ruling for data centers imminent
topSignals.text: FERC held its monthly open meeting on June 18 with Agenda Item E-1 (Docket RM26-4-000) — the long-awaited ruling on interconnection of large loads (≥20 MW) to the interstate transmission system. The Commission may issue a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking or a final order. Pre-meeting stakeholder positions show two camps: (a) DOE proposal and utilities/PIOs favor 100% network upgrade cost assignment to the large load developer; (b) hyperscalers (Google, Microsoft, OpenAI, Meta) and the Data Center Coalition support expedited pathways with thresholds raised to 75–200 MW. RTOs (PJM, MISO, SPP) push for regional flexibility. A "developer pays 100%" outcome raises effective cost of grid-connected data center power by $10–50M+ per 250 MW project, structurally strengthening SOFC behind-the-meter economics. Ruling text expected at ferc.gov/rm26-4 later today. (White & Case: FERC June 2026 Agenda Summary; FERC docket)

topSignals.title: Google confirmed as Project Jade customer; Tallgrass replaces Crusoe, project "full steam ahead"
topSignals.text: Bloomberg (reported via Blockspace) identified Google as the customer behind the 1.8 GW Cheyenne, Wyoming data center campus that triggered Crusoe's exit. Google raised concerns about costs and construction timetable; Tallgrass Energy is now sole developer and confirmed operations proceeding "full steam ahead." Google contributed $200M+ in refundable construction contributions. Phase 1 targeted mid-2027; service to Google by early 2028. Planning documents show Bloom Energy fuel cells alongside Tallgrass natural gas generation infrastructure. This resolves the customer identity monitor flag from the June 16 digest and largely removes the headline overhang on Bloom's Cheyenne-linked pipeline. (Blockspace: Crusoe pushed out by Google; Cowboy State Daily: project continues)

topSignals.title: Bloom Energy board grants CEO KR Sridhar 271K performance PSUs; market cap at $79B (8-K June 17)
topSignals.text: Bloom's board approved 271,076 performance-based restricted stock units for CEO KR Sridhar on June 15, tied to multi-year aggregate revenue targets with a mandatory hold until December 31, 2031. Market cap: ~$79B, up from ~$5B at end-2024 (+1,480% in 18 months). Signal: board's 5-year lock-up on a revenue-linked grant indicates internal conviction that AI data center fuel cell demand supports sustained multi-year growth, not a transitory spike. (Minichart: Bloom 8-K June 2026)

lcoe.text: FERC cost-allocation outcome — SOFC BTM advantage quantification (pending ruling today): If FERC adopts 100% developer-pays network upgrade cost assignment, grid-connected data center power in PJM faces: $500K study deposit + $15K/MW readiness + 100% network upgrade costs ($10-50M per project). For a 250 MW project: $3.75M deposits + $10-50M network upgrades upfront — structurally widening the SOFC BTM cost advantage for US East Coast/Midwest deployments. If ruling is a NOPR, watch for comment deadline ~Q4 2026. (White & Case: FERC Agenda)
